_comment: Address encoding parameters for the coins the wallets will hold natively.
DERIVED FROM EACH CHAIN'S OWN DAEMON, not copied from a wiki. For each coin
an address was minted by the coin's own binary in a throwaway offline
datadir, base58-decoded, and its checksum verified; `wif` came from
dumpprivkey on that same address. A version byte copied from a third party
and off by one produces addresses that look plausible, pass no checksum
anyone else recognises, and lose whatever is sent to them.
`p2pkh` and `wif` are facts about the chain and are safe to rely on.
`bip44` IS NOT A FACT — read the warning on each entry before using it.
MEWC is absent on purpose: its daemon was mid initial-block-download and
could not mint an address, and guessing its byte is exactly the mistake
this file exists to avoid. Re-run the derivation once it is synced.
_bip44Warning: A DERIVATION PATH IS A COMMITMENT, NOT A DETAIL.
Change it after anyone has received coins and their balance reads zero —
the funds are still on-chain, at addresses the wallet no longer derives.
And if the path does not match what the coin's OWN wallet uses, a user who
imports their existing seed sees an empty wallet and reasonably concludes
Several of these coins have no registered SLIP-44 coin type that could be
confirmed, so the path below is left null rather than filled with a
plausible number. Each one needs checking against that project's own
wallet before it ships — ideally by importing a seed into both and
comparing the first address. That check is cheap; getting it wrong is not.

PEP.name: Pepecoin
PEP.note: watch strategy: an address is only tracked from its first query; see services/coin-esplora.

DINGO.name: Dingocoin
DINGO.note: 0x1e/0x9e are Dogecoin's own bytes, which is expected of a Dogecoin fork — and is also why a DOGE address will validate against this chain's rules. The wallet must not treat them as interchangeable.
